thread:
alex: Trying something ridiculous today — ironing board as a standing desk + I taped my kid's finger-painting to the wall behind me for morale. pic: https://imgur.com/a/placeholder.jpg 

emily: Legendary. toddler-curated wallpaper is peak WFH decor :laughing: 

alex: Also, my ISP keeps dropping for ~30s every hour. Anyone here using mesh + powerline? apartment wiring is ancient. 

matt: Ironing board FTW. For flaky wiring, powerline adapters can help but avoid running through surge protectors/extension cords — plug straight into the wall. 

rachel: Also try a cheap mesh node near the line-of-sight between the modem and where you work. It cured my attic ghost-coverage. 

alex: Speedtest from right after a dropout: 
```
Ping: 23 ms
Download: 12.3 Mbps
Upload: 1.1 Mbps
Packet loss: 3%
Traceroute: 10.0.0.1 -> 172.16.0.1 -> 198.51.100.1 (loss on hop 3)
```

lena: That packet loss on hop 3 looks like ISP side. Run `mtr -r -c 50 8.8.8.8` and paste results if you want, but likely open a support ticket with those numbers. 

emily: Same apartment + different floor — had recurring 1-2 minute drops, ISP replaced the ONT and it stopped. 

alex: Ugh, ONT replacement. Worth trying a full modem+router power cycle first. Also gonna try swapping the coax connector (it was loose on the closet end). 

matt: If you go powerline, get a pair that supports passthrough and AES — they actually perform ok for zoom/meet. 

rachel: Poll: everyone vote — background ambience for working: 1) white noise 2) lo-fi 3) toddler orchestra (true) 

alex: 3) obviously :joy: 

lena: 2) 

emily: 1) when focus needed, 3) when trying to survive a napless afternoon 

ops-bot: Reminder: maintenance window on ISP integration tests tomorrow 03:00-03:30 UTC (no customer impact expected). :gear: 

alex: Thanks — I'll try a power cycle + test another outlet tonight and report back. Appreciate the tips y'all :party: 

matt: Also post a before/after pic of the ironing-board rig. we demand evidence. :camera:
